chunks: My father narrated (may God be pleased with him) who said: Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: I admonish you against two characteristics, in which those who perished perished: Beware of giving fatwa to people based on your own opinion, or basing your religion on what you do not know.

key_terms.بِمَا لَا تَعْلَمُ: on what you do not know

ai.seo_question: What are the two characteristics that lead to spiritual ruin according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) warns against two specific pitfalls in religious authority: relying on subjective personal opinion (*ra'y*) for fatwa and practicing a religion based on incomplete or erroneous knowledge. This distinction highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on rigorous epistemology, where valid jurisprudence requires deep understanding rather than mere speculation, ensuring that religious practice is grounded in authentic divine guidance.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 2-66 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Ali ibn Ibrahim ibn Hashim quoted Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, on the authority of Yunus ibn Abdul-Rahman, on the authority of Abdul Rahman ibn al-Haj’jaj

that Abu Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) told him, “I admonish you against two characteristics which can ruin men: to worship God with a wrong religion, and to advise people on issues you are uninformed about.”
